recommendation.recommendation: Implement immediate supplemental irrigation to relieve critical water stress during the flowering stage.
recommendation.justification: Satellite NDVI shows excellent canopy health, but high NDWI and SAVI indicate severe water stress and soil exposure, compounded by 7‑10 days without precipitation. Immediate irrigation will prevent wilting, reduce disease risk (e.g., Fusarium wilt), and protect the current yield potential while leveraging the existing strong vegetative vigor and optimal soil conditions.
actions: Activate flood irrigation today to bring soil moisture to field capacity (≈32% volumetric water content).
Apply an additional irrigation pulse (10‑15 mm) within the next 24 hours to simulate rainfall and address the 7‑10 day deficit.
Schedule irrigation every 7‑10 days thereafter, adjusting volume based on soil moisture sensor readings and upcoming weather forecasts.
Apply a balanced N‑P‑K fertilizer (medium nitrogen) concurrently with irrigation to support nutrient uptake under high canopy demand.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Restored soil moisture will alleviate water stress, maintain canopy photosynthesis, limit disease onset, and preserve the projected yield and profitability for the current cotton crop.
monitoring_plan: Daily soil moisture checks (sensor or gravimetric) to ensure moisture stays above wilting point (14%).
Weekly NDVI/NDWI satellite updates to verify reduction in water stress levels.
Bi‑weekly visual scouting for wilt symptoms (yellowing, leaf droop) and pest presence.
Track SAVI values monthly to monitor soil exposure and adjust irrigation to prevent erosion.
Review weather forecasts each morning to anticipate natural rainfall and modify irrigation schedule accordingly.

Soil conditions are optimal (pH 6.25, medium nitrogen, loam texture) and the canopy health (NDVI 0.75) is excellent, meaning the crop can recover quickly if water is supplied. The combined evidence points to irrigation as the only action that can prevent wilting, disease risk, and yield loss.
